content:
Sara: heads-up — Elm customer LoRA merge done, quickpack run for int4 quant shows a recurring numeric formatting regression on invoice lines. attaching top-level observations.
Mike: can you paste the quickpack summary?
Sara: TL;DR: fp16 baseline vs int4 quantized (post-merge) — conversational quality fine, but structured fields (invoice numbers, amounts) get scrambled in ~12% of cases.
Sara: eval snippet:
```
Model: elm-lora-v2 (merged)
Baseline fp16 structured-acc: 0.988
Int4 quant structured-acc: 0.866
Top failure class: invoice_number_format (12.1%)
Example failure: "Inv # 00456" -> "Inv # 4 5 6" (token splitting)
```
Anjali: ugh, tokenization + quantization interaction again. Is this using our new per-tensor 4-bit group size?
Sara: yes — group_size=128, qtype=awq. Also ran with group_size=64 and saw drop to 9.8% (still bad).
Nina: any quick hypotheses? tokenization offset? special tokens?
Mike: please share a failing prompt and tokenizer debug output. might be a merge-order weights stitch issue.
Sara: failing prompt example:
```
Customer: Please show invoice #00456 from March.
Model: Sure — Invoice # 0 0 4 5 6 dated 2025-03-12.
```
Sara: tokenizer.debug for "#00456": tokens ["#", "00", "456"] in fp16, but int4 path yields ["#", "0", "0", "4", "5", "6"] when run through the quant runtime.
Kai: that suggests KV cache or attention rounding causing extra splits during generation. Can we repro offline with deterministic sampling (top_k=1, temp=0)?
Sara: did that — deterministic still shows split on int4. I ran a quick LUT compare of logits around the split token and saw a tiny perturbation pushing argmax to different tokenization boundary.
Anjali: could be kernel selection fallback. Which kernel was used?
Sara: runtime log: chosen kernel=matmul_q4_awq_fast_group128, fallback=none.
Nina: try transiently forcing the group64 kernel with memcpy to check. also try merging weights with float32 requantize step (remap via fp16->int4 pipeline) to see if it's a merge artifact.
Mike: also run a quickpack that compares generation under three paths: (A) fp16 baseline, (B) int4 standard merge, (C) int4 merge + post-quant remap. include exact-match for invoice tokens.
Sara: starting that now. attaching run id: quickpack/elm/1742123456/01
deploy-bot: Model elm-lora-v2-int4 deployed to shadow pool eu-west for pack quickpack/elm/1742123456/01 :package: :eyes:
Sara: quick results (summary):
- A: fp16 structured-acc 0.988
- B: int4 standard 0.866
- C: int4 remapped 0.965
So remap reduces failures drastically.
Anjali: ok that points to quantization during merge as root cause. We should add a remap step in the customer onboarding flow.
Kai: note CPU runtime cost for remap is nontrivial; add a perf smoke to ensure latency delta < 5% for 1k token bursts.
Nina: also check tokenization vocab compatibility between base and LoRA. maybe LoRA introduced a small embedding shift. run dot-product similarity on token embeddings for the affected tokens pre/post-merge.
Sara: I ran a quick sim: avg cosine(#00456 tokens) before merge 0.9992, after merge (pre-remap) 0.987 — small but apparently enough.
Mike: next steps: 1) add automated quickpack test that asserts structured-acc >= 0.98 for customer Elm; 2) add remap to onboarding pipeline as opt-in; 3) investigate possible kernel-level mitigation (group64 default?)
Anjali: I'll file the onboarding PR to add remap option and the quickpack gate.
Sara: filed PR draft: github.com/redwood/elm-onboard/pull/42 — includes tests and perf script.
Mike: great. leave this thread when PR merges. thanks all. :thumbsup:
